description: Round-1 FIND-004 ('stale/contradictory seller-agent manifest+README') was fixed only in coral-agents/seller-agent/coral-agent.toml and coral-agents/seller-agent/README.md. The higher-level, judge-facing examples/txodds/coral/README.md — the exact directory SUBMISSION.md's 'one command a judge can run' points a judge at — was left internally self-contradictory: its architecture diagram still shows the pre-R5/R6 shape (WANT service=txline, AWARD to=seller-worldcup, settlement=arbiter, ARBITER_RELEASED), and its env-var bullet list never mentions SELLER_KEYPAIR_B58, ANICCA_TELEMETRY_URL, ANICCA_DASHBOARD_URL, CLAWROUTER_URL, or LLM_PROVIDER=clawrouter — while the SAME file's later prose correctly states SETTLEMENT_MODE=direct is now this fork's default and documents the docker-build-first gotcha. A judge reading this file top-to-bottom hits a direct contradiction (arbiter vs direct; txline vs anicca) that FIND-004 was supposed to eliminate fork-wide, not just in one sub-package.

evidence.snippet:
buyer-agent
  -> WANT service=txline arg="edge <fixtureId>"

seller-worldcup   -> BID price=0.00045  specialist
...
buyer-agent
  -> AWARD to=seller-worldcup
  <- ESCROW_REQUIRED reference=<bound-order-hash> settlement=arbiter
  -> DEPOSITED settlement=arbiter vault=<vault PDA>
  <- DELIVERED {teams, odds, LLM/fallback read}
  -> ARBITER_RELEASED sig=<devnet tx>

contradictingEvidence.snippet: this fork's .env defaults to SETTLEMENT_MODE=direct — a real 2-party buyer-released escrow — because a freshly setup.js-generated ARBITER_KEYPAIR_B58 is NOT the on-chain admin arbiter...
